# Feature Fields

Also called: Generalized NeRF, Semantic Fields

## Overview
Feature Fields generalize the standard Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) formulation by predicting arbitrary per-point feature signals $\mathbf{f}$ in addition to volume density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ [S1, unofficial]. This extension allows the 3D representation to encode semantic labels, physical properties, or latent embeddings from 2D foundation models, enabling tasks such as zero-shot segmentation and scene editing [S1, unofficial]. Unlike standard NeRF which only models appearance, this family lifts 2D observations into a consistent 3D representation by supervising the rendered features against 2D feature maps [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism modifies the radiance field function $F_\Theta$ to map input coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ to a tuple $(\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{c}, \sigma)$, where $\mathbf{f} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a feature vector [S1, Parent, unofficial]. The rendering of these features follows the same volume integration principle as color [G]. For a ray $r$, the rendered feature $\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r)$ is computed as:

$$
\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{f}(x_i)
$$

where $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ is the accumulated transmittance and $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$ is the opacity weight [S1, Parent, unofficial]. Supervision is performed by comparing the rendered feature $\hat{\mathbf{F}}(r)$ against ground-truth 2D feature maps or teacher network outputs projected onto the image plane [S1, Parent, unofficial]. This process lifts 2D observations into a consistent 3D representation [S1, Parent, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Multi-Space Neural Radiance Field (MS-NeRF)](11707-multi-space-neural-radiance-field-ms-nerf.md)
Addresses reflective/refractive objects by using parallel sub-spaces.

### [NRFF](12072-nrff.md)
Encodes view-dependent effects using multiscale tensor decomposition and Anisotropic Spherical Gaussians.

### [Semantic and Feature Branches](12095-semantic-and-feature-branches.md)
Adds a general feature branch to predict arbitrary high-dimensional vectors for diverse downstream tasks.

### [NeRF for Object Segmentation](12404-nerf-for-object-segmentation.md)
Targets probabilistic occlusion masks using "area encoding" for view-consistent segmentation.

### [Semantic-NeRF](14889-semantic-nerf.md)
The first work to explicitly integrate semantic information using a dedicated direction-independent semantic branch supervised by categorical cross-entropy.

### [Augmented Features (Avg, Var, Color)](15000-augmented-features-avg-var-color.md)
Enhances representation by explicitly injecting mean, variance, and color aggregates into the feature field.

### Object Field Representation
A function $f(\mathbf{p})$ that maps a 3D point $\mathbf{p}$ to an object code vector $\mathbf{o}$, representing object ownership independent of viewing angles [S2, unofficial]. The object code $\mathbf{o}$ is defined as $H+1$ dimensional, where $H$ is a predefined maximum number of solid objects the network predicts, and the last dimension represents empty space to handle occlusion and collision [S2, unofficial]. The function $f$ is parameterized by a series of MLPs [S2, unofficial]. A pitfall is the variable number of objects and large non-occupied volumes, solved by fixing the dimension to $H+1$ [S2, unofficial].

### N3F
A method that learns additional feature fields to realize self-supervised 3D segmentation [S3].

### NeRF Branch Feature Sampling and Augmentation
Variance of color features describes occupancy: low variance implies occupied 3D location (Lambertian assumption), while high variance implies free space (different appearances from different views) [S4]. Points are sampled along the ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t \times \mathbf{d}$ [S4]. Augmented features are computed by sampling from multi-view image features (typically $160 \times 120$) instead of low-resolution volume features ($40 \times 40 \times 16$) to address aliasing [S4]. The augmented feature $\bar{V}$ is a concatenation of $\{V_{avg}, V_{var}, \text{RGB}_{avg}, \text{RGB}_{var}\}$ [S4]. Density and latent features are computed as $\sigma(\mathbf{p}), \hat{\mathbf{h}}(\mathbf{p}) = \text{G-MLP}(\bar{V}(\mathbf{p}), \gamma(\mathbf{p}))$, and color as $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{p}, \mathbf{d}) = \text{C-MLP}(\hat{\mathbf{h}}(\mathbf{p}), \mathbf{d})$ [S4]. Sampling from image features achieves 20.51 PSNR for novel-view synthesis compared to 18.93 with volume sampling [S4].

### Feature Sampling from Multi-View 2D Features
Sampling point features along the ray from multi-view image features instead of low-resolution volume features to address the need for high-resolution images in NeRF [S4]. This approach achieves 20.51 PSNR for novel-view synthesis compared to 18.93 with volume sampling [S4].

## Background
The concept of feature fields generalizes the NeRF formulation, which originally maps $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\mathbf{c}, \sigma)$, to predict arbitrary per-point feature signals $\mathbf{f}$ [S1, unofficial]. Semantic-NeRF was the first to introduce semantic fields within the NeRF framework, using ground-truth semantic segmentation maps to augment the radiance field with per-point semantic logits [S1, unofficial]. Subsequent works have extended this to include physical properties, latent descriptors from 2D foundation models, and object codes [S1, S2, unofficial][S3].
